newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Brotherhood to boycott elections.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Brotherhood to boycott elections.

text.p: Jordan's powerful Moslem Brotherhood said on Wednesday it would boycott parliamentary elections scheduled for November.
The Brotherhood, whose Islamic Action Front (IAF) political arm is the country's largest parliamentary opposition party, said the decision was taken by its consultative council.
"The Moslem Brotherhood council decided to boycott the upcoming 1997 parliamentary elections," said a terse statement issued after a meeting late on Tuesday night.
Brotherhood head Abdul-Majid al-Thuneibat, who signed the statement, said the movement would issue a detailed explanation of its decision later.

The elections are scheduled to be held by November this year but no date has been officially set. In the last elections in 1993 the Islamic Action Front won 16 of the 80 seats in a parliament filled with small pro-government parties and tribal representatives.

But the IAF failed to block ratification of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, which the Islamists want cancelled, and supporters of the boycott said it was time to pull out of a parliament which they said they could not influence.

"Even if there are (Islamist) parliamentary members they are weak because at least 60 deputies of the 80 represent the government," Islamist deputy Abdul-Moneim Abu Zunt said this week. He also said the elections might be rigged in favour of pro-government candidates.
But opponents of the boycott said that without parliamentary representation, the Islamists would lose their influence and their political party would become redundant.
